item.title: Inside Victor Wembanyama's search for a go-to move
item.description: Victor Wembanyama, de los Spurs de San Antonio reacciona después de encestar un triple durante la segunda mitad del juego de baloncesto de la NBA frente a los Bulls de Chicago, el miércoles 11 de noviembre de 2026. (AP Foto/Nam Y. Huh) (Nam Y. Huh/Associated Press) Victor Wembanyama was still 15 years away from being born when Kareem Abdul-Jabbar unfurled the final skyhook of his Hall of Fame career in 1989. But the Spurs' 7-foot-4 phenom has watched enough of Abdul-Jabbar to understand the enduring power of what was once basketball's most devastating scoring weapon. More Information NBA defenses beware: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama is searching for a signature shot The footage is grainy. The shorts are short. And the shot is still impossible to defend. "That kind of move is unstoppable," Wembanyama said. "I mean, people knew Kareem was going to that skyhook. It still worked." As the Spurs' 22-year-old centerpiece works to refine an offensive game still brimming with untapped potential, he isn't necessarily trying to invent the next skyhook. His search for a go-to move - something dependable, something repeatable, something to call upon when the Spurs absolutely, positively need a bucket - is a journey all his own. And not one that can be rushed. "Players to this day in the league, the great ones have signature moves like that," Wembanyama said. "I'm just saying if it has to become a signature move, it should be naturally. You have to trust the game." The NBA's history books are littered with go-to moves that became as much a part of basketball lore as the players who perfected them. George Gervin had the finger roll. Dirk Nowitzki had his one-legged fadeaway. Tim Duncan, never one for much pomp and circumstance, made a career out of banking shots off the glass. Hakeem Olajuwon - a player Wembanyama has trained with during each of the past two offseasons - had his Dream Shake. So what will Wembanyama's go-to move be? San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) shoots over Golden State Warriors forward Gui Santos (15) during the third quarter of an NBA Cup basketball game at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. The Spurs defeated the Warriors 123-85. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) For now, that remains a work in progress. "I think it's a constant conversation," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "We want to just try to make sure we can get the best shot in every possession." The need for such a weapon isn't merely theoretical. In the closing seconds of the Spurs' Oct. 30 loss to Houston, Johnson turned to Wembanyama for a potential game-tying basket. Amen Thompson had other ideas, stuffing Wembanyama's left-handed attempt at the rim. Asked afterward if he would have changed anything about his approach against the 6-foot-7 Thompson, Wembanyama answered in the affirmative. "I would have dunked," Wembanyama said. item.title: Drake Maye could miss rest of season after suffering lower leg injury, reports say
item.description: FILE - New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (10) is sacked by Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (97) during an NFL football game in Munich, Germany, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. (AP Photo/Lennart Preiss, File) Lennart Preiss The New England Patriots could be without quarterback Drake Maye for the rest of the season. Maye suffered a significant lower leg injury during Sunday’s game against the Lions in Germany, according to multiple reports. ESPN and NFL Network reported that Maye suffered a serious injury that could keep him sidelined for the remainder of the season. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported Monday that a source described Maye’s injury as a “significant lower leg injury” that will keep him out for an extended period. Rapoport said Maye and the Patriots will seek additional medical information after returning to the United States. Maye was injured when he was sacked during the Patriots’ first drive of the game. He was initially considered questionable to return but was later ruled out. Before the Patriots left Germany, head coach Mike Vrabel said Maye was unable to continue playing. “He couldn’t, couldn’t function, couldn’t play, couldn’t run, couldn’t do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute or function at that level,” Vrabel said. “I know that it was a lower leg injury. I don’t know the exact details of it, but I know he couldn’t go back in.” The Patriots have a bye this week before facing the Chargers in Los Angeles on Nov. 29. This is a developing story. item.title: ‘I heard’: Journalist shares what Bayern talked about Lennart Karl future
item.description: ‘I heard’: Journalist shares what Bayern talked about Lennart Karl future Bayern Munich youngster Lennart Karl is a special talent, but he recently faced public criticism from the club’s honorary president Uli Hoeneß. The 18-year-old made a breakthrough into the first-team under Vincent Kompany last season, and scored nine goals and registered eight assists across all competitions. He finished three places below Lamine Yamal in the Kopa Trophy (best young player), and has a bright future at Bayern. What Bayern think about Lennart Karl View this post on Instagram While many people acknowledged the Bayern winger’s drop in form, there were others who were unhappy that such thoughts have been made public. Christian Falk has exclusively told CFBayern Insider that Bayern are happy with the player’s development, but handing him a new contract is not currently on the agenda. The club are waiting to see what Michael Olise decides about his future, and once his situation is sorted, there will be more clarity on Karl. The Bild journalist said : “Lennart Karl is a very special person at 18 years of age. As journalists, we often say everything is really quiet and really boring when it comes to interviewing players these days because everyone is so media-trained and giving the same answers. Lennart Karl is not like that, and he doesn’t play like that either. He also doesn’t wear clothes like that! He was at the Ballon d’Or ceremony, having finished three places below Lamine Yamal in the Kopa Trophy (best young player). He has a big future in the sport, which other clubs are no doubt aware of, and certainly Bayern are wary of the wandering gaze from their European rivals. “I heard there was an internal meeting where Bayern talked with the Lennart Karl side. They told him that he’s a very important player for Bayern Munich and that they’re very happy with his development. But they weren’t so happy that they were prepared to talk about a new contract! He’s still earning a salary of about €2.5m gross [£2.08m]. So, you see, there’s a lot of space there to work with in future. Everyone is now waiting for a decision from Michael Olise. When this decision is made, everyone will be able to see things more clearly around Lennart Karl and his future at Bayern Munich.” Lennart Karl needs to step up with key players injured (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images) This is an important season for Karl, and he can shut down his critics with strong performances. Michael Ballack, the player’s agent, certainly was not happy with the comments directed at the youngster. Karl has registered three goals and two assists across all competitions this season, and he will be aiming to improve the numbers. With Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry currently out injured, Karl is expected to feature heavily after the November international break.

item.title: Versatile Barcelona defender still absent from group training as key midfielder makes progress ahead of Villarreal clash
item.description: Versatile Barcelona defender still absent from group training as key midfielder makes progress ahead of Villarreal clash Barcelona have yet to welcome Jules Kounde back to full team training, leaving Hansi Flick with another fitness concern ahead of Sunday’s La Liga meeting with Villarreal on November 22. According to SPORT , the French defender was still working separately when the squad resumed training on Monday, November 16, despite hopes that the international break would give him enough time to recover from his left ankle sprain. It is to be noted that Kounde has now spent a month recovering from the injury sustained against Real Betis on October 17. What initially appeared to be a relatively minor setback has developed into a longer absence , with persistent discomfort preventing the defender from returning to normal training. Jules Kounde is still not training with the group. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images) On the other hand, however, there is more encouraging news concerning Dani Olmo, although Barcelona will also need to assess his response to training before confirming his availability against Villarreal. Kounde’s recovery takes longer than Barcelona expected Barcelona initially anticipated that Kounde would miss approximately a week after spraining his left ankle against Betis. However, the defender continued experiencing discomfort even after the initial inflammation subsided, which complicated his recovery. The international break offered an opportunity to complete his rehabilitation without the demands of competitive matches, but his continued absence from group training suggests that the final stage of recovery has proved more difficult than expected. Dani Olmo provides a boost after recovery Barcelona are hoping Dani Olmo could return from his injury against Villarreal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Olmo’s situation offers a more positive development for Flick, as the midfielder has been working towards a return after suffering a grade-one tear in his left adductor during Barcelona’s Champions League meeting with Paris Saint-Germain. It must be remembered that his initial recovery estimate was approximately one month. His progress has been encouraging, with Barcelona targeting the Villarreal fixture for his return . However, a lot still depends on progressing through rehabilitation and eventually receiving medical clearance, mostly becuase has still has not completed a full group training session yet.

item.title: Vinicius admits contract uncertainty and transfer interest affected Real Madrid form: ‘I’m human and I make mistakes’
item.description: Vinicius admits contract uncertainty and transfer interest affected Real Madrid form: ‘I’m human and I make mistakes’ Speaking at a press conference, Real Madrid megastar Vinicius Jr. has admitted that uncertainty over his Real Madrid future and interest from other clubs affected his preparation and subsequently his form during the early stages of the season. The 26-year-old winger has endured a difficult start to the 2026/27 campaign under Jose Mourinho, managing a paltry return of just one goal and three assists in 12 appearances. Vinicius has also missed four La Liga games this term due to suspension following his direct red card against Villarreal last month. Vinicius opens up on difficult start Discussing his difficult start to the campaign ahead of Brazil’s friendly against Singapore, the Real Madrid attacker pointed to a combination of personal and professional factors behind his struggles. “I don’t think I prepared myself in the best way after the World Cup , because the impact of being eliminated was very big for all Brazilians,” he started. “Losing so early was something we didn’t expect. I used the holidays to rest, disconnect, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years,” Vinicius added. The forward also acknowledged that uncertainty surrounding his future at the Bernabeu took a mental toll. “All of that could have affected my start to the season. So could my contract renewal and the fact that many clubs were interested in me last summer. It all affected me a lot mentally, as did the situation at Real Madrid. But the season is very long,” he noted. Struggling. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) The Brazilian then went on to acknowledge that maintaining an elite level of standards over prolonged periods is not always easy, while calling legends Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi as exceptions. “Maintaining such a high level for so long is very difficult. I think only Cristiano Ronaldo and Messi have managed it for so many years, putting up the same numbers,” he said. “I’m human and I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve . I try to understand football and the day-to-day better, but I’m 26 years old. I also have to enjoy life a little.” Vinicius backs himself to come good Despite his disappointing opening months, Vinicius insisted that his current scoring record should not be viewed in isolation, pointing out that he went through a similarly unproductive spell last season before finishing with more than 20 goals. “Until December I had only scored five goals and then I finished with more than twenty, as in the rest of the seasons. I am preparing myself and evolving because in the most decisive moments of the season I am always there,” he noted. The forward also addressed criticism of his performances for Brazil, taking responsibility for the national team’s recent struggles. item.title: Canada issues update on Alphonso Davies injury
item.description: Photo by Getty Images | Getty Images Bayern Munich star Alphonso Davies started his first Canada match in a long time on Friday against Guatemala, captaining the side and hoping that he would be able to last a full 90 minutes on the field for his na tional team for the first time in around two years. It was not to be, however, as after just 5 minutes he slipped in an attempt to block a shot and quickly signaled that he could not continue. Despite Davies’ later proclamation that he could have theoretically stayed on the field, doing so was deemed an unnecessary risk, and he was taken off immediately . A diagnosis o f the Canada star’s injury has taken some time, but the country’s football federation released this update on the matter, via Joshua Kloke of The Athletic : Following a medical scan today in Toronto, it has been confirmed that Alphonso Davies sustained a minor lower-body muscle strain. He is travelling back to Germany, where he will continue to receive ongoing care. Given that Davies said he felt something off in his hamstring during the first Canada training session—and considering his recent history of injuries—the likelihood is that the former Vancouver Whitecaps player’s lower-body muscle strain is a hamstring strain. If this is the case, we can look at the recovery time one requires for such strains. A minor hamstring strain usually takes around 1 to 3 weeks to heal, though the Bavarians will likely wish to be very careful with Davies’ recovery. Again, he has a long history of such injuries. This is far from an ideal situation. But at least it was not an ACL tear, right? (Knocks furiously on wood) Join the conversation! item.title: ‘I’m gonna…’ – What Aaron Rodgers said after throwing an interception shows he’s ready to retire
item.description: Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers suffered a brutal loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, and the all-time great QB had far from an all-time great performance. Rodgers had a poor performance against the Bengals, while his counterpart on the other side, Joe Burrow, had a historic outing to help his team get the win. In his final year, many fans had hoped that Rodgers would be able to turn back the clock and deliver a farewell season for the ages. Aaron Rodgers couldn’t hide his frustration after getting picked off During the second quarter on a third down, Aaron Rodgers threw a 20-yard pass that was intercepted by Cincinnati Bengals Safety Jordan Battle. After the play, Rodgers could be seen mouthing the words “I’m gonna f****** quit!” after his errant pass was picked off by the Bengals. Overall, Rodgers did not have a good game, throwing for 143 yards and two touchdowns, getting sacked three times for 25 yards and fumbling the ball once. It was a performance that showed that Rodgers, who was once the best quarterback in the NFL, is no longer the elite performer he once was. That isn’t a knock on his talent or his greatness. Unfortunately for Rodgers and many other ageing athletes, Father Time is undefeated and has now caught up to him. The Steelers are still in playoff contention, as this loss moves them to 6-3, behind the Bengals in second place in the AFC North standings. Even if the Steelers do reach the playoffs, they aren’t expected to be a massive threat to reach the Super Bowl, especially given how stacked the AFC is right now. The Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Cincinnati Bengals, and the Kansas City Chiefs are all teams still considered considerable favourites to emerge from the AFC in February. Hopefully, Rodgers can turn his form around in the next game and see out his final season in the NFL in the best way possible. item.title: 'Not competitive' Brazil can improve, insists Ancelotti
item.description: Carlo Ancelotti faced criticism in Brazil after the Selecao lost 3-2 to Japan (Roslan RAHMAN) Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti on Monday promised an improved performance in the year-ending clash against Singapore, admitting that his squad was "currently not competitive." The Selecao lost 3-2 against Japan in a friendly in Singapore on Saturday, where Ancelotti and skipper Raphinha were red-carded after Japan scored the dramatic clincher in stoppage time. "Given that the team is currently not competitive, I want to do more," Ancelotti told reporters in Singapore, where Brazil play on Tuesday. The Italian, Brazil's first-ever permanent foreign coach, said: "I want to do more because I enjoy being here, so that the team can become more competitive on the global stage. "The priority is to play well first (tomorrow) and to do well." Ancelotti, 67, is coming under increasing pressure, following a string of underwhelming performances including two defeats, two wins and a draw in Brazil's last five international outings. Japan avenged a 2-1 defeat by Brazil in their previous meeting at this year's World Cup, when the South Americans beat them in a round-of-32 clash. After Saturday's loss, Ancelotti faced a barrage of criticism, including from former Brazilian national team star Romario. Ancelotti brushed off Romario's remarks, saying "like anyone he has the right to express an opinion." But the former Real Madrid coach, who reacted with fury after Brazil appealed for a foul in the build-up to Japan's winning goal on Saturday -- which was upheld by VAR -- said that his team "didn't deserve to lose" against Japan. Japan face Paraguay on Tuesday in the second match of the double-header at Singapore's National Stadium. str-jhe/gj

item.title: YouTube Gold: When There Was No Dunk
item.description: American varsity basketball player Lew Alcindor (later known as Kareem Abdul-Jabbar) of UCLA during a game against University of Southern California, Los Angeles, California, 1967. (Photo by PhotoQuest/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s probably very hard for fans today to understand how dominant Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, then known as Lew Alcindor, was when he was at UCLA. First of all, though freshmen weren’t eligible, almost everyone stayed for four years. For the three years he was on the varsity, Kareem won three national championships and led UCLA to an 88-2 record over those three years. And in one of those games, against Elvin Hayes and Houston, he had an eye injury. He was so dominant, in fact, that the NCAA did something they’ve only rarely done: they changed the rules because of a specific player. Like Bill Russell, whose dominance led to the goaltending rule, and Wilt Chamberlain, who forced the NCAA to widen the lane and to require that foul shots be taken from behind the line. (Chamberlain had a habit of taking off from behind the foul line and dunking), the NCAA made a major rule change for Kareem: they outlawed the dunk. They cited other reasons, but everyone knew. However, the rule backfired in a big way: deprived of the easiest shot for an athletic big man who was vastly more talented than his opponents, Kareem began to practice the Mikan Drill relentlessly (the Mikan drill, named for George Mikan, is where you do a left-handed hook shot, then one with the right). Ultimately, this evolved into the single-most deadly shot in the history of the game and, quite possibly, the most devastating single offensive weapon in the history of sports. The rule was finally repealed in time for the 1976-77 season. During those years, fans missed seeing not just Kareem dunk, but also players as great as Julius Erving and David Thompson. item.title: ‘This is not the way’: Family speaks out after elite college soccer twins detained by ICE
item.description: Demonstrators gather in Hingham Square on Wednesday, Jan. 14, 2026, to protest policies on immigration, Greenland, ICE and President Donald Trump. They began the weekly Stand Up Speak Out! protests in 2025. Twin brothers Luis and Carlos Orta-Santoro were heading back to Wallace State Community College in Alabama, where they play soccer, after spending the weekend with their parents in Georgia earlier this month. But they never made it back to campus. The 19-year-old Venezuelan twins were pulled over in a small Alabama town, and they’ve been in ICE custody ever since. Now, their family is speaking out, with their mother insisting that her sons are not criminals and that “this is not the way” to handle immigration enforcement. Traffic Stop Turns Into ICE Detention According to the twins’ father, Carlos Enrique Orta Corredor, an officer in Lincoln, in Talladega County, stopped the brothers for allegedly failing to come to a complete stop at a stop sign. Orta Corredor told WBRC that the officer asked for their driver’s licenses and then told them that they were undocumented immigrants. Both brothers were reportedly removed from the car, handcuffed, and taken to a police station. They spent the night in the county jail before being handed over to ICE the next day. Lincoln police signed a task force agreement with ICE in July, according to The Cullman Tribune . Those agreements allow local officers to use limited immigration authority during routine police work, though booking records don’t say whether the officer who stopped the brothers was acting under it. The family came to the United States from Venezuela because of safety concerns tied to the political situation in their home country. Their parents say the twins have valid driver’s licenses, work permits, and immigration documents, and the brothers have a pending asylum case. The twins were first held in Alabama, but they’ve since been moved to the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in Louisiana, which is exactly what their family had been hoping to avoid. ‘This Is Not the Way’ The twins’ mother, Reyna Santoro, made it clear that she doesn’t think her sons should be treated like criminals. “They are young men who just turned 19. That doesn’t mean they are criminals. I agree that criminals should be taken away, absolutely, but this is not the way,” Santoro said, via WBRC. Their father also spoke about how stressful the situation has been for the family. “We have to be extremely careful because even when you haven’t done anything wrong, you can still find yourself going through these situations, this difficult time, this mistreatment, this agony,” Orta Corredor said. Santoro also asked for help getting their elected officials involved, hoping to keep her sons from being moved to Louisiana. “My appeal is for people to help us reach our representatives, our congressmen and senators. item.title: “Just Criticizing For The Sake Of Criticizing Now” – Carlos Alcaraz Fans Blast Andy Murray’s Brother For Questioning Spaniard’s Entourage Size
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz. © Imagn Carlos Alcaraz’s loyal fans have openly criticized Andy Murray’s brother, Jamie, for taking a swipe at the Spaniard’s entourage. Jamie, a doubles specialist in his playing days, took a dig at the size of Alcaraz’s entourage, wondering why the former World No. 1 Spaniard needs so many people to travel with him. Currently, Alcaraz is in Turin for the year-end ATP Finals. Jamie is covering the prestigious event as a pundit for Sky Sports Tennis. Here, the former men’s doubles World No. 1 said : “Obviously over the years, it’s been a thing about having the physio, the strength conditioning trainer, the agent, the nutritionist, the doctor, all that stuff and it’s packed right? It’s packed. For me, it’s too much. You see Alcaraz in the gym before the match and there’s six people standing around just watching him on a foam roller. What world are we living in?” Several Alcaraz fans objected to what Jamie said and took to X (formerly Twitter) to criticize the Brit. One fan wrote: (translated from Spanish via Grok) “This is just criticizing for the sake of criticizing now. Clearly, Andy Murray is much smarter and more elegant than his brother.” Carlos Alcaraz to get ATP Finals campaign underway with Round Robin phase clash against Frances Tiafoe Alcaraz is slated to lock horns with Frances Tiafoe of the USA in his first match at the 2026 ATP Finals. The Spaniard is the favorite on paper to win the prestigious year-end event this year given his rampant form in the buildup to the tournament, which included title triumphs in Tokyo, Vienna and the Paris Masters. However, Alcaraz has never won the ATP Finals, and the closest he came was last year, when he fell to Jannik Sinner in the final. Against Tiafoe, the Spaniard should be confident but cautious. Alcaraz leads the head-to-head 2-1 , with the American’s only win in the rivalry having come way back in 2021 at the Barcelona Open. However, their subsequent matches were five-set thrillers, with Alcaraz narrowly edging their 2022 US Open and 2024 Wimbledon clashes. item.title: Belgium's all-time record goalscorer Romelu Lukaku retires from international football at 33
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-BEL-TRAINING - AFP Belgium’s greatest-ever goalscorer Romelu Lukaku has officially announced his retirement from international football at the age of 33. The legendary striker calls time on a Remarkable 16-year career with Belgium, confirming he is at peace with the decision to step away from the national team setup. A legendary international career concludes Lukaku has sent shockwaves through the Belgian football community by confirming his departure from the international stage. The 33-year-old forward, who has long served as the focal point of Belgium’s "Golden Generation," revealed his decision on Sunday following a career that spanned more than a decade and a half. His exit marks the conclusion of a significant chapter for the national team, as they lose their most prolific attacking weapon in history. The announcement follows a period of speculation regarding the striker's long-term future under the current management. Lukaku remained an unused substitute during Belgium’s recent victory over Italy , a match where Mark van Bommel’s side secured a convincing win. Despite his influential role behind the scenes during that fixture, the forward has decided that now is the appropriate moment to hang up his boots for his country, leaving a void that will be incredibly difficult for the next generation to fill. Reflecting on his lengthy journey in the national shirt, Lukaku shared a poignant message with his followers on social media. "16 years," he began his announcement on Instagram . "These 16 years i gave all i had for the national team… i went through Evert emotion possible… I played with amazing teammates that i will always be grateful for. I want to thank them all.. i want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team.. it was a nice ride and i enjoyed every single moment," as quoted by HLN . Gratitude for the Belgian supporters Lukaku’s relationship with the Belgian fanbase has seen various highs and lows throughout the years, yet he leaves with a sense of deep appreciation for those who stood by the squad. His career highlights include leading the line through multiple major tournaments, establishing himself as a symbol of Belgian football’s rise to prominence on the global stage. He made sure to specifically address the fans who traveled across the world to support the team during his tenure. "To the belgium fans thank you for the support you gave our team.. i am proud to have represented my country in 4 world cups and 3 european championships.. I will never forget those moments i’m at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable. I’m grateful. Thank you," the striker added in his final international statement. item.title: “Totally Unacceptable Coaching and Preparation”: Fans Want Brian Schottenheimer to Take Responsibility As He Blames Defense for Cowboys’ Loss
item.description: Brian Schottenheimer. © DallasCowboys.com Brian Schottenheimer has tested the patience of Dallas Cowboys fans multiple times, and Sunday was no exception. After his Dallas Cowboys lost 46-40 to the San Francisco 49ers on that day, the head coach blamed the defense, which allowed 584 offensive yards, including 214 on the ground, for the result during his postgame presser: “Totally unacceptable defense. … The tackling was atrocious. … You can’t give up three explosive plays of over 65 yards for touchdowns and expect to win in this league. … I have never been around a situation like this. We rushed the passer well, got five sacks. But what is killing us is missed tackles and explosive plays. … Can’t do that.” Fans disagreed with his take: Offensively, Dak Prescott had a commanding performance, throwing for five touchdowns – three of them to George Pickens – but also an interception. However, the Cowboys failed to get their run game going, generating just 96 yards. The 49ers, meanwhile, had a more balanced offense. Christian McCaffrey and Deebo Samuel accounted for five touchdowns (three receiving and two rushing), and rookie Kaelon Black also rushed to the end zone once. Brian Schottenheimer praises Dak Prescott, George Pickens despite Cowboys’ loss to 49ers Speaking of Dak Prescott and George Pickens, Brian Schottenheimer singled them out for their heroics in the same presser: *“The fight, the finish. What can you say about Dak? He got hit a bunch early. Maybe the greatest competitor I’ve ever been around. Awesome to have George back doing George [Pickens] things. At the end of the day, we didn’t score enough points to win.”* He continued: “We’ve been very inconsistent. Win one, lose one, win one, lose one. But the fight is right; I do agree with that.” The Cowboys host the Tennessee Titans a week from now in their next game. Kickoff is at 12 p.m. CT on Fox. item.description: Romelu Lukaku made his Belgium debut in 2010 (JOHN THYS) Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku on Monday retired from international football after scoring 94 goals in 135 games for his country, saying he was "at peace" with his decision. Lukaku featured in four World Cups for the Red Devils and helped them reach the quarter-finals of this year's tournament before losing to eventual winners Spain. The 33-year-old, who now plays for Turkish club Fenerbahce, made his debut in 2010 as a teenager and was an unused substitute in Sunday's 4-1 Nations League win over Italy. "These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team. It was a nice ride and I enjoyed every single moment," Belgium's record goal scorer said on Instagram. "To the Belgium fans, thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships. "I will never forget those moments. I'm at peace with my decision to stop here," Lukaku said. The former Chelsea, Manchester United and Inter Milan forward was part of Belgium's so-called 'golden generation'. Lukaku, alongside Kevin De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, finished third at the 2018 World Cup, a best-ever finish for Belgium in the tournament but they failed to lift a trophy during the period. "I played with amazing teammates that I will always be grateful for," Lukaku said. "I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team," he added. - 'Legend, my brother' - A host of fellow Belgian players paid tribute to Lukaku. "Legend, my brother," midfielder Axel Witsel said on Instagram. "Thank you for everything my bro," Courtois said. "So many amazing memories," the Real Madrid goalkeeper added. Lukaku's last appearance for his country came in October's 4-1 loss to France. "Beyond his exceptional performances on the pitch, he has been a true leader, with a strong personality and an essential role in the dressing room," Lukaku's former team-mate and now Belgium's technical director Simon Mignolet said in a statement from the Belgian football association. "We respect his decision and are deeply grateful to him for everything he has brought to our national team," the former Liverpool goalkeeper added. Belgium's first game without Lukaku will be a Nations League last-eight fixture in March. "We must now turn our attention to the future and prepare for the Nations League quarter-finals," Mignolet said. "With the ambition of continuing to make progress as a team," he added. mad/ec/iwd/gj

item.title: Takeaways from Georgia's 48-21 win over Missouri
item.description: The No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs (9-1, 7-1 in SEC) picked up a third straight dominant win against a ranked SEC opponent, thumping the formerly No. 22 Missouri Tigers 48-21 . The Bulldogs were leading 41-7 by the middle of the third quarter before the Tigers started to put things together in garbage time. Georgia gained 468 total yards of offense, nearly 200 more than Missouri on the day (286) and they were incredibly balanced, with 286 yards through the air and 182 yards on the ground. Extremely fast starts The Georgia Bulldogs have executed the principle of starting a game well to a tee in this game. They scored points on all five of their first possessions, amassing a 31-0 lead over Missouri with 6:47 left to go in the half. By that point, Georgia had more touchdowns (four) than Missouri had first downs (one). The Bulldogs have been able to do this all season. In fact, they've amassed a 21+ shutout lead in seven games this season. However, the first four games were the wins against Tennessee Tech (35-0 lead, 63-3 win), Western Kentucky (49-0 lead, 70-20 win), Arkansas (21-0 lead, 45-17 win), and Oklahoma (28-0 lead, 41-13 win), so people doubted they can do it against better competition. However, their last three games have shown that the Bulldogs can. Florida was ranked No. 17 by the AP Poll when they faced Georgia on Halloween, and the Bulldogs led 24-0 by halftime on their way to a 27-8 win. They travelled on the road to play a No. 10-ranked Ole Miss team that had a spot in the College Football Playoff, and the Bulldogs had a 35-0 lead before Ole Miss scored their first point. Georgia won 42-7. It's one thing to beat great opponents, but to do it in the way that Georgia's beating them. Gunner Stockton's efficiency Gunner Stockton has been very efficient in his last two games. Against Ole Miss last week, he threw for 186 yards and four touchdowns in just 15 attempts. In this game against Missouri, he threw for 252 yards and a touchdown in 24 attempts. That's two games in a row with over 10 yards per attempt, and it's the sixth game he's had over 10 yards an attempt this season. He didn't have a single game last season where he's had over 10 yards an attempt, and this season he's had one in more than half of his games. With the Heisman buzz he was getting last season, there will surely be more votes coming his way after this season. When you can run the football, you can do anything Still, I doubt Stockton would be as efficient and effective as he was without his running game. They're playing at a different level right now, and the Missouri game showed another great performance. Lead back Nate Frazier had 72 yards and three touchdowns (a hat trick) on 14 attempts. Dwight Phillips had 66 yards on seven attempts. Chauncey Bowens had a touchdown on his only run. Even Craig Dandridge ripped off a 22-yard run on an end around. item.title: Browns are 6-4 with Andrew Berry, Deshaun Watson escaping thin ice. Opinion
item.description: CLEVELAND — Andrew Berry’s job as Browns general manager and Deshaun Watson’s status as a starting quarterback were on life support heading into the 2026 season. But Jimmy and Dee Haslam stuck with Berry and Watson , even though logic suggested the opposite would be wise, and the Browns owners have been rewarded with a team exceeding every reasonable expectation as its Week 11 bye begins. Against all odds, the Browns are 6-4 after overcoming a 17-point deficit and defeating the Houston Texans 27-24 on Sunday, Nov. 15, at Huntington Bank Field. The six victories — which include a 4-0 start at home for the first time since 1963 — mean the Browns have hit the over on 5.5 wins, just like Jimmy Haslam boldly predicted they would during a training camp news conference on July 31. Todd Monken deserves a huge chunk of credit for the turnaround he has overseen in his first season at the helm of the Browns, who went 5-12 in 2025 during the last of coach Kevin Stefanski’s six years in charge. However, the Browns would not be in this position if Berry and Watson had not simultaneously executed Houdini acts. Berry has drafted extremely well the past two springs after assembling five consecutive lackluster classes, three of which did not include a first-round selection because of the controversial Watson trade made with the Texans (3-6) in March 2022. Ownership could have fired Berry when it ousted Stefanski on Jan. 5, but Berry bought himself more time with his moves in 2025. Watson has orchestrated six fourth-quarter game-winning drives in 2026 after he entered this season 9-10 as a Browns starter, with abysmal performances, an 11-game suspension stemming from sexual assault and sexual misconduct allegations made during his Texans days and injuries combining for what had been widely considered the worst trade in NFL history. On the heels of a season-opening 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Browns were ready to bench Watson in favor of Shedeur Sanders if Watson didn’t play well in Week 2, though he bought himself more time with a 23-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. item.description: A sense of normalcy has returned to State College, and if Penn State can capitalize on a favorable end-of-season schedule, then the team will be flying high heading into 2027. The Nittany Lions are riding a three-game winning streak after Saturday’s 42-14 takedown of Minnesota . Although the wins haven’t been perfect, it’s very promising that head coach Matt Campbell has found a way to overcome Big Ten competition after losing his first four games in the conference this year. The team has nearly punched its ticket to December football, so these final two games against teams with losing records should be close to pressure-free for Penn State. There was likely a lot of angst and tension in the building for weeks as the Nittany Lions tried to end their four-game losing streak, but all of those feelings should be gone now. With mostly everything trending in the right direction for them, let’s look at the biggest storylines they are dealing with this week. Man down Running back Carson Hansen had his best game of the season against Washington — and then he proceeded to one-up himself on Saturday against the Golden Gophers . He had 12 carries for 126 yards and a touchdown in the first half, but he suffered an injury close to half time and never returned. Nobody knows the extent of the injury yet, but hopefully it isn’t anything too serious. The offense is already missing wide receiver Koby Howard , so it would be difficult to overcome losing Hansen as well, especially with how well he played in the last two games. Unlikely outcome Penn State’s chances of making a Bowl Game were murky at best after a four-game losing streak to begin Big Ten play. But after a three-game winning streak to make their record 6-4, the Nittany Lions will likely be playing football next month. While they could potentially earn a trip without another win this season, taking one of these last two games would be helpful to securing a more prestigious Bowl Game. It’s important for Penn State to impress as many people as possible down the stretch in hopes of beginning the 2027 season as a ranked team. Boredom breeds creativity Penn State will be going up against a couple of teams near the bottom of the Big Ten — Rutgers and Maryland — in the final two games of the season. With a Bowl Game appearance all but locked up, the coaching staff could look to experiment since they have some room for error. They can use these last two games to test out new personnel groupings, trick plays, and they can even try to get some guys on the field who haven’t played much this year. The Nittany Lions should win at least one of these games handily, so they would be wise to look for some more advantages. item.title: Tiverton girls volleyball completes perfect season with D-III title
item.description: PROVIDENCE — Tiverton girls volleyball had one goal this year. A veteran cast returned for the Tigers after a championship loss. A repeat ending couldn’t happen — Tiverton wouldn’t allow it. The Tigers raced through the regular season undefeated and reversed their Rhode Island College fortunes. No. 1 Tiverton swept No. 10 North Providence, 25-16, 25-14, 25-23, for the Division III crown on Sunday night at the Murray Center. The Tigers’ championship hopes were ended in three sets against Ponaganset last fall. This heavy senior-led group achieved their lone goal and earned the school’s first title since 2017 and fifth overall on November 15. “This feels amazing,” Olivia Rodrigues said. “It's obviously my last season, and I've grown up with these girls. We played four years with each other, and we're good friends outside of volleyball. It's a really great feeling. “We went into the year wanting revenge. We wanted to come out strong, and this is exactly what we wanted.” Tiverton (19-0) immediately became a title favorite when realignment pushed a few of the league’s top teams into D-II. Being the preseason favorite was welcomed, but following through on such expectations adds pressure. The Tigers never felt threatened and started the year with four straight sweeps. They finished with 18 straight-set matches across the regular season and playoffs. They only lost four sets all year and never went to a fifth frame this season. The Tigers went 54-13 over the last four seasons and reached at least the semifinal round in three of those years. They were due for a win at this stage and didn’t let it slip away. Watch RI games on NFHS Network all season “It's like such an unreal feeling, especially after last year,” Adysson Amaral said. “We worked our butts off for this, so it just feels so nice. They're just my family, so excited. It’s my last season ever, but it's just the best feeling that we wanted.” Olivia Pereira provided the winning kill after North Providence rattled off a late run and nearly stole the set. But Pereira, one of nine seniors on the squad, ended it after a perfect set from Sayler Ouellette. Tiverton started the opening frame on a 5-1 run and never trailed in the set. The second frame was more of the same with Amaral providing consecutive aces at the onset, while Pereira dominated on the outside. The lead ballooned to 23-13 after separate 5-0 and 7-0 sequences. “Definitely bittersweet because we're all the seniors will be leaving, but we wanted to come back and win this, and we did,” Pereira said. “We're all very happy.” The Tigers had the loudest crowd of the day. item.title: ‘We all fell in love with him’ – Hull coach shares what Lewis Koumas was like behind the scenes
item.description: ‘We all fell in love with him’ – Hull coach shares what Lewis Koumas was like behind the scenes A member of the coaching staff at Hull City has spoken very highly of what Lewis Koumas was like behind the scenes during his loan move at the MKM Stadium. The Liverpool striker spent the second half of last season with the Tigers, playing a part in their promotion to the Premier League with three goals in 18 Championship appearances (including the play-offs). He’s since become a fixed first-team player at Anfield, being handed five starts among his 14 appearances across all competitions and scoring in the Champions League victory over LASK in October. Everyone at Hull ‘fell in love with’ Koumas Hull assistant coach Dean Holden spoke to The Redmen TV about how Koumas immediately won people over with his humility and hardworking attitude. The 47-year-old said: “Within a week, everyone fell in love with him, from Stan on the door, the security guy, to the kitchen staff, kit men, the lot. We all fell in love with him. “You know why? Just because he’s a real humble lad who just wants to be the best he can be and affects people around him in an energetic manner and just loves football.” Holden went on to share anecdotes of Koumas being out on the training pitch along with Joe Gelhardt ’20 minutes out before everyone else is in the gym’, telling coaches not to ‘sugarcoat’ advice to him, and waiting patiently for his mother to collect him after he scored a late winner for Hull on his debut against Blackburn instead of ‘going out on the town and celebrating’. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Koumas appears to have a sky-high ceiling While we’re sure that the Liverpool youngster has been helped by sage advice from his father Jason, who graced the Premier League with West Brom and Wigan, the onus is still on him to put all of that bequeathed wisdom into action, and he’s most certainly doing that. Andoni Iraola clearly has plenty of faith in the 21-year-old if he’s playing him regularly, even starting him against Manchester City (albeit that Alexander Isak wasn’t fit), and the young striker is repaying that trust with his performances on the pitch. John Aldridge voiced his belief that the Wales international will ‘ play for Liverpool for a long time ‘, with Koumas standing out for his indefatigable pressing in the final third, which carries echoes of the beloved Bobby Firmino. The stories shared by Holden testify to the tremendous attitude of the Reds youngster, who’s remained grounded and earned his place in the first-team squad to the extent that he’s nudged Federico Chiesa further down the pecking order. We’re sure there’s still so much more to come from the Welshman, provided he can maintain the traits which have taken him this far already and (fingers crossed) avoid any major injury issues.

item.title: Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction
item.description: Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That’s a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn’t sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there’s still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein’s first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Game Info Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers’ playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it “not a good plan offensively or defensively,” and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. item.title: Giannis to get a Milwaukee Brewers World Series ring. He's an owner.
item.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo is getting a Milwaukee Brewers World Series ring. The Brewers are in the process of designing the rings for the owners, players and staff, which means the former Milwaukee Bucks star is included in that list. "Everybody who's an owner would be getting a ring," said Brewers president of business operations Rick Schlesinger said. "Sure. He's an owner." Before the playoffs, Antetokounmpo went on his brother's Thanasis' podcast, the Thanalysis Show, and gave some advice to the Brewers. "Enjoy. Don't let the outside noise infiltrate the locker room," Antetokounmpo said. "You guys have started something months ago together... when we won the championship there was so much outside noise coach (Mike Budenholzer) used to say don't ever get too high, don't ever get too low. "And when we win a game, people are going to say how amazing you are, it's not true. And when we lose a game, they're going to say you're the worst. It's not true either. Just stay even." 🚨 Giannis Antetokounmpo has a message for the Milwaukee @Brewers ! 🔥⚾️ “Keep on knocking on that door. Eventually that door will BREAK…” #Brewers #NLDS #MLB pic.twitter.com/k9OtWRprFp — Thanalysis Show (@ThanalysisShow) October 2, 2026 Antetokounmpo became a minority owner of the Brewers in 2021 after the Bucks won their first championship in 50 years. Antetokounmpo saw some parallels with the 2021 team and the Brewers. "I know there's going to be a lot of pressure because they've always been good. We were in the same position. We were always good winning in the regular season but wasn't able to win in the playoffs," Antetokounmpo said. "I always believed if you stayed consistent, you keep on knocking on the door, eventually that door will break. And I think the Brewers have done this for many years and eventually that's going to happen. Back in 2021, Antetokounmpo said his representatives reached out to Attanasio in 2020 when the Bucks were in Orlando playing in the playoffs in the "bubble" during the coronavirus pandemic. Antetokounmpo was looking for other ways to be involved in the Milwaukee community. “There’s no better way to start than with the Milwaukee Brewers," Antetokounmpo said in 2021. "We want to win a championship here. It’s going to take time and patience but we have a great ownership group, we have great players and we’re going to accomplish it with a lot of hard work." Five years later, Antetokounmpo is now playing with the Miami Heat after the Bucks traded him during the summer. The Brewers are currently in the process of designing the ring. "There is a relatively short window of time to get the rings designed because production of the rings is something that is done by hand and it takes a long time," Schlesinger said. "You want to make sure the rings are available for our players and our front office staff when the season starts in 2027." item.title: Roma finalize permanent deal for Balerdi
item.description: Roma finalize permanent deal for Balerdi Leonardo Balerdi has quickly become an important player for Gian Piero Gasperini. Upon his arrival, the Grugliasco-born coach called him one of the new captains, given that he wore the captain’s armband at Marseille. Born in 1999, the defender arrived on loan from OM, and the buyout is contingent on the defender’s appearances. To trigger the €11 million obligation, Balerdi will have to play 40% of the matches. The figure increases if he makes more appearances: €14 million, with over 55% of matches lasting at least 45 minutes. The former Marseille player could be satisfied with just 20% of the matches in the second half of the season. In this case, Roma would have to pay the French club €9 million. Gasperini considers him an important player, and in a short time, he’s carved out a significant niche for himself, considering the starting lineup alongside Mancini, Ndicka, and Hermoso: 639 minutes, highlighted by a brace away to Napoli. As La Gazzetta dello Sport reports, if an automatic buyout were to arrive, all the conditions are in place for this to happen: the Giallorossi club and the player are already in full agreement regarding the contract renewal. In fact, the parties have already put everything down in black and white. The desire of all is to continue together.
